title: Stirling PDF — Discovery
script: Before uploading a private PDF, check whether you can do the job locally. Stirling PDF brings merging, splitting, compression, OCR, and other PDF operations into one workspace. Its project describes desktop and self-hosted options. Choose the actual local setup before making a privacy claim. The project is open core. That means the license and paid feature boundaries deserve a look. For me, the useful question is whether the exported file is right, especially after redaction. Next: seven real jobs against Acrobat. Which one would you test first?
timingStatus: Aligned to actual Voicebox recording with local recognized word timestamps. Minor unrecognized tokens interpolate between recognized neighbors.
concept: Merge, split, compress, OCR, redact and reorder in one workspace.
whyNow: A practical alternative deserves a current, version-specific check before a viewer changes workflow.
viewerGoal: Decide whether this recorded workflow fits their own devices, plan and needs.
hooks: Before uploading a private PDF, check whether you can do the job locally.
Can this PDF job stay on your computer?
A PDF workspace needs more than a feature count.
strongestHook: Before uploading a private PDF, check whether you can do the job locally.
directorBrief: Direct this as a useful discovery with one important limit: Merge, split, compress, OCR, redact and reorder in one workspace. Keep real app interaction dominant. The final verdict depends on who can use the tool for this recorded workflow, not a universal winner. Capture version, OS and plan so the evidence can be interpreted.
effort: 30–90 minutes capture/test; large transfers and export waiting may add elapsed time.
protocol: Use a local desktop or self-hosted setup supported by current Stirling docs. Capture exact version and mode, official license and available features. Use synthetic PDFs only. Demonstrate merge, split and one additional installed operation, then open output independently. Any claim of local processing must be tied to actual chosen setup and relevant docs; hosted service access is not proof of offline privacy.
evidenceRequirements: Verify actual local processing, free limits and open-core licensing.
